patterns.text: Bare for about 81 days each farming year, from 31 Mar to 19 Jun.
Rice at mid-season faced heat in 8 of the last 10 seasons.
Reference evapotranspiration is falling since 1991, a statistically clear trend in NASA POWER data (82.9 mm per decade).
Water stored on land in this region (~300 km) has fallen about 3.94 cm per year since 2002 (GRACE/GRACE-FO).

grace.note: Total water stored on land. The satellite measurement covers about 300 km. Public NASA JPL Analysis Tool subsets for the demo cells. Separate gain factors were unavailable.

evidence.name: Rice and wheat
evidence.verdict: This is your current rotation. Every other option is compared with it.
sources: PAU Package of Practices Kharif 2026 / Rabi 2025-26
assumptions_L: A soil arrow needs a difference of at least 2 points in a season. An arrow changes when the option wins or loses in at least 16 of 24 seasons.
Bare soil uses a crop coefficient of 0.25 after at least 5 mm of rain or irrigation in 3 days, and 0.10 otherwise.
A crop is heat-hit after 3 hot days in its flowering window. The frost threshold, when applied, is 2 °C.
The heavy-rain index uses rain events of at least 12.7 mm. Local slope is omitted.
The soil score averages six indicators of field practices. Newly reached soil is assumed to start at field capacity.
The residue model uses the time between crops. Residue machinery multiplies predicted burning pressure by 0.3.
The water arrow compares water use by crops and soil, with a 3% threshold in each season. Irrigation pumping is shown alongside it.
For crops outside ponded rice, the model assumes 60% of pumped water reaches the crop roots and tests 50% to 75%.
The model assumes 200 mm of water for puddling over 7 days (150 to 300 mm range). It tests rice field drainage from 2 to 15 mm/day.

why: This rotation is the baseline for the season-by-season comparison.
evidence: Replayed through 24 real seasons (2001 to 2024) of NASA POWER weather.
Median soil score 29.6 (range 23.3 to 34.4) vs 29.6 now. Water used by crops and soil 1123 mm/yr vs 1123 mm/yr.
benefits: Compare the soil factors and the season counts below.
gaps: Disease and nutrient balance are not modelled.
Income is not modelled. Check local prices.
risks: Rice faced heat at flowering in 20 of 24 seasons.
Check this with your local agriculture office or extension service (for example a Krishi Vigyan Kendra in India) before changing your rotation.

why: The Punjab crop calendar leaves room for summer moong between wheat harvest and rice transplanting.
evidence: Replayed through 24 real seasons (2001 to 2024) of NASA POWER weather.
Median soil score 51.4 (range 42.4 to 55.7) vs 29.6 now. Water used by crops and soil 1428 mm/yr vs 1123 mm/yr.
benefits: Legumes host bacteria that pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, so the next crop may need less fertiliser.
Living roots and leaves protect bare soil from sun, wind and heavy rain, and feed soil life.
Adds a harvest you could eat or sell. Check local prices.
The score for days with living roots rose from 0.71 to 0.89.
The score for time with nitrogen-fixing crops rose from 0.00 to 0.54.
The score for crop families rotated (breaks pest and disease cycles) rose from 0.00 to 0.60.
gaps: Disease and nutrient balance are not modelled.
Income is not modelled. Check local prices.
risks: Rice faced heat at flowering in 18 of 24 seasons.
Summer moong faced heat at flowering in 24 of 24 seasons.
Check seed availability and the time needed to prepare the field between crops.
Check this with your local agriculture office or extension service (for example a Krishi Vigyan Kendra in India) before changing your rotation.

why: Maize fits the summer crop slot and avoids puddling the field for rice. The rotation keeps wheat in winter.
evidence: Replayed through 24 real seasons (2001 to 2024) of NASA POWER weather.
Median soil score 52.5 (range 43.4 to 57.7) vs 29.6 now. Water used by crops and soil 929 mm/yr vs 1123 mm/yr.
benefits: Leaves or stalks can feed livestock.
The score for crop residue kept, not burned rose from 0.50 to 0.93.
The score for no puddling (puddling compacts a hard layer under the topsoil) rose from 0.00 to 1.00.
gaps: Disease and nutrient balance are not modelled.
Income is not modelled. Check local prices.
risks: Maize faced heat at flowering in 22 of 24 seasons.
Check this with your local agriculture office or extension service (for example a Krishi Vigyan Kendra in India) before changing your rotation.

validation.note: GGCMI rice spans 06-29 to 11-26. Winter wheat spans 11-04 to 04-16. These dates overlap here. Rice, wheat and the Punjab moong window require 378 crop days before any gaps.
